title: Service Siren — Evacuation Lane Scratchpad
content:
Context and purpose:

Quick personal scratchpad for a lightweight emergency routing and version pinning strategy I want available in my head during late-night anomalies. I call this the "Evacuation Lane": a fast, low-friction path to get customer traffic off an at-risk model variant and onto a predictable, safe fallback (could be a smaller model, a cached response, or a static heuristic) while we triage. This doc is not a polished runbook; it's my working thoughts + command snippets and thresholds to try in the field.

Goal (1-liner):
Give SREs/engineers a 2–3 step low-risk sequence to divert traffic within 60–120s with minimal config changes and a deterministic rollback path.

Assumptions:
- Canary / staged rollout is in place for normal deploys. Evacuation Lane is for when telemetry shows severe functional regression (error spike, hallucination surge, cost runaway) that standard canary thresholds didn't catch or when traffic pattern suddenly changes.
- We have a routing layer that supports per-model pins, per-tenant overrides, and quick percentage splits via the console/API.
- We maintain a small set of always-available safe variants: stable-1.3 (quantized), safe-lite-embedder, and fallback-static-heuristic.

High-level triggers (metrics that should make you consider opening the lane):
- Real-time error rate (5m) > baseline * 4 AND absolute error rate > 0.8%
- Latency p95 jump of > 2x for 2 consecutive 5m windows
- Quality regression alert from eval hooks: BLEU/ROUGE drop beyond threshold or flagged eval prompt set failure rate > 10%
- New reports from support about coherent user-impacting issues (DM/Slack + ticket).

Evacuation lane steps (fast path):
1) Signal: raise "siren" channel (Slack #evacuation-siren) and @oncall. Short message: "Siren: model x.y.z > error spike 11:32 UTC. Opening evacuation lane. Diverting new traffic to stable-1.3 for affected routes." Include quick link to dashboards (latency, errors, tokens).

2) Apply immediate routing override (API): prefer per-route pinning where possible. Priority order (choose one based on scope):
   - tenant-level (if only certain tenants affected) -> pin tenant model to stable-1.3
   - route-level (specific API route) -> override route to safe variant
   - global (all traffic) -> disable variant x.y.z and move default to stable-1.3

   CLI examples (placeholders):
   - pin tenant: curl -X POST https://console.api/v1/overrides -d '{"scope":"tenant:acct-123","model":"stable-1.3"}' 
   - route override: redwoodctl routes override --route /v1/generate --model stable-1.3 --reason "evacuation-lane"

3) Reduce attack surface: throttle batch sizes and disable optional tool-calling on the diverted traffic to keep latency and inference reliability predictable (if runtime supports flags).

4) Observe for 10–20 minutes. If metrics improve, keep in place and start a controlled investigation (see triage checklist below). If not, escalate to load-shedding: further force traffic to fallback-static-heuristic (graceful degraded UX) and engage pager.

Fallback ground rules (how and when to move to static fallback):
- If after 20 minutes diversion metrics do not return to acceptable bounds OR error pattern looks systemic (infrastructure/driver-level) -> move to fallback-static-heuristic.
- For fallback, prefer route-scoped changes to avoid breaking unaffected tenants. Document user-visible change in status page.

Version pinning considerations (quick heuristics):
- If incident is a downstream model artifact (e.g., model weights corruption or bad quantization), pin to last-known-good commit (git-sha) and create a dedicated tag (e.g., stable-1.3-pin-2026-02-14).
- Avoid heavy surgery during high-traffic hours. Prefer moving traffic first, then fixing artifact.
- Keep the pinned artifact immutable; attach a short audit note with time and reason.

Triage checklist (10–20m, short investigations you can perform while lane open):
- Are errors stack traces hinting at runtime kernel failures? (GPU OOM, kernel mismatch) -> infra oncall.
- Are hallucination/quality issues correlated with specific prompt templates or token-length distribution? -> product/ML.
- Is the increase in token cost or latency due to sequence length or changes in batching? Check batching metrics.
- Review model binary/quantization commit history for recent merges in last 24–48h.
- Check if traffic pattern shifted (e.g., bot flood, data with long contexts).

Communication snippets (short, copyable):
- Initial siren: "Siren: opening evacuation lane for model x.y.z due to error rate spike. Diverting affected routes to stable-1.3. Investigating. ETA 30m for next update."
- After divert success: "Update: evacuation lane active; p95 latency and user error rate back to baseline. Investigating root cause, keeping traffic pinned for stability. Triage owners: @name."
- Escalation to fallback: "Escalation: metrics not improving. Moving to fallback-static-heuristic for minimal user disruption. Incident page: <link>."

Quick rollback / un-evacuate guidance:
- Don't unpin until sanity window of 30 minutes of stable metrics after fix is validated on canary traffic (not just single request tests).
- To reintroduce, prefer phased re-introduce: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 50% over 30–60 minute windows, monitoring semantic-eval hooks for regressions.

Edge cases & gotchas:
- Client-side SDK caching of model ID: some SDKs pin model ID at session creation; even after routing override, active sessions may continue to hit the old variant. Solution: expire sessions or force SDK toggle if possible.
- Per-tenant warm caches: diverting a tenant to a quantized stable model may cause cold-start behavior; consider warmup cohort for heavy tenants if time permits.
- Telemetry lag: dashboards are sometimes 30–60s behind. Use real-time logs and sample golden requests to confirm.

Open questions (things to decide later / document properly):
- Should evacuation lane auto-close after N minutes with gradual unpin, or require explicit human confirmation? (I lean explicit confirmation for now.)
- How to best surface SDK-level session pinning in the console to warn SREs when a tenant will not respond to routing change immediately.
- Should we maintain a separate small fleet of ultra-stable quantized nodes for evacuation traffic to avoid impacting normal capacity pools? Cost vs reliability tradeoff.

Notes to self (playbook refinements I want to try):
- Add a console button that opens a guided flow: 1) pick scope, 2) pick fallback, 3) add audit note, 4) send siren message template.
- Add a real-time test harness: after override, auto-send 5 golden prompts and show diff of outputs to console for a quick sanity check.
- Track how often we use evacuation lane per month and root cause categories in a tiny spreadsheet (for follow-up).

Immediate TODOs (if you are me at 3:14am and seeing this):
- Draft the siren slack template and pin it in #ops-runbooks.
- Add a short runbook snippet to confluence linking to this scratchpad.
- Ping @Priya to discuss console button mockup when not oncall.

End of scratchpad. Keep this as my lightweight memory aid; convert to a proper runbook if the pattern repeats 2x in the quarter.
